look_here_first: Start with the woody base and leaf texture. Rock penstemon is a low densely branched subshrub with thick dark-green leathery leaves that have coarse mucronate teeth. It grows from limestone cracks and carries red tubular flowers on short stalks.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: densely branched with lower stems becoming woody

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves small, thick, leathery and dark green

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf margins coarsely serrate, teeth often mucronate

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: corolla red to rosy red, roughly 25–30 mm, tubular/bilabiate

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: white inner throat heavily marked with dark guide lines

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: specialized for dry limestone crevices, bluffs and canyon walls

lookalikes.differences: Penstemon triflorus: P. triflorus is herbaceous rather than woody-based and has thinner, larger opposite leaves. Penstemon cobaea: P. cobaea is a broad-leaved herb with enormous pale flowers, not a woody cliff subshrub. Penstemon tenuis: P. tenuis is a slender wet-site herb with tiny lavender flowers and soft thin leaves.
